public_rationale: The antecedent occurred: Reka raised a large round while pre-revenue. Subsequent records show product adoption and paying subscribers at the examined startups, which matters against a reading that they would never sell anything. They do not establish the financial independence emphasized in the surrounding passage. Character.AI's October 2026 bankruptcy is consistent with the concern about sustainability, but one company's distress cannot settle a categorical forecast about the cohort. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule.
limitations: The result depends on interpreting functional business in light of the passage's emphasis on independence from financing.
Revenue growth, product use and additional funding cannot substitute for operating cash-flow evidence.
No deadline or exhaustive company list was supplied.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Pre-revenue AI startups that raise large funding rounds are not real companies. They have no chance of becoming functional businesses, and VCs hope to sell them on to other companies or to retail investors.
conditions: AI companies with no revenue raising large rounds

statement.excerpt: These are not real companies (real companies make money and sell things), but symbolic items that venture capitalists hope can be sold to other companies or credulous retail investors because there isn’t a chance in hell they become functional businesses.

from_speaker: real companies make money and sell things
venture capitalists hope can be sold
there isn’t a chance in hell they become functional businesses
our_interpretation: These refers to the pre-revenue AI startups raising large rounds described immediately before this sentence, including Character.AI and the linked Reka example.
Read the categorical forecast as saying that none of this cohort will become commercially self-sustaining.

Functional business means sustained customer receipts sufficient to support ordinary operations without recurring outside financing. This follows the surrounding discussion of independence from further funding; merely launching a paid product is insufficient.
No specific profit measure, accounting basis or financial threshold is supplied. This is assessed as a business-viability forecast, not a numerical earnings forecast.
The statement about hoped-for exits concerns investor intentions. An eventual sale alone would not prove that this was the original motive.
No deadline is supplied, and the cohort is not an exhaustive named list.
criteria.support_condition: Conclusive evidence establishes that every member of the identified cohort permanently ceased operating without ever becoming commercially self-sustaining. Failure of one example does not establish the categorical claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one demonstrably qualifying startup develops sustained customer-funded operations that no longer depend on recurring outside financing.

evidence.explanation: The report states that Reka raised $50 million and had no revenue, establishing a qualifying company before the post. The funding is attributed to the companies and the pre-revenue status to an unnamed informed source.

Reka describes actual product use and announces additional financing in the same disclosure. Neither establishes whether customer receipts cover operating costs; raising money also does not prove that it is necessary for survival.

evidence.locator: CEO discussion of monetization before Growth vs. Safety
evidence.explanation: The CEO reports growth in paid subscriptions, countering a reading that these companies could never sell anything. The interview supplies no proof that customer income sustainably covers operating costs.

The company announced bankruptcy while continuing service and seeking a buyer. This is evidence of distress, but neither a completed shutdown nor proof that every qualifying startup can never become self-sustaining.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reliable financial records showing sustained customer-funded operations at any qualifying startup would contradict the forecast. Supporting the entire forecast would require an exhaustive cohort and evidence that every member permanently failed without achieving that state.
